title: Schema Guardian: converged telemetry merger and drift-detected backfill for per-request inference KPIs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Prometheus scrapes and OTLP exporters produce overlapping, slightly divergent signals for the same inference requests (latency, token counts, error codes). This causes duplicate rows in billing and noisy SLOs when consumers join datasets. We need a converged collection layer that produces a single canonical per-request KPI envelope, detects schema/cardinality drift, and backfills missed envelopes with a watermark-aware replay.

Scope: implement a Schema Guardian service that: 1) accepts OTLP and Prometheus-adapted ingress, 2) canonicalizes labels and metric names to the internal KPI contract, 3) attaches trace/request context (trace_id, request_id, model_variant) via tracing hooks, 4) performs tenant-aware adaptive sampling with deterministic retention for high-value routes, 5) emits deduplicated envelopes to downstream KPI store and to a low-latency events topic for realtime dashboards.

Non-goals: not a replacement for long-term metric archival or full trace storage; we will not change customer-facing metric names in this work.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Schema Guardian service ingests both OTLP and Prometheus-origin traffic and emits a single canonical envelope per request (latency_ms, token_in, token_out, error_code, model_id, variant, region, tenant_id, trace_id, request_id).
2) End-to-end tests validate deduplication across inputs with >99.9% correctness on synthetic collisions.
3) Drift detector emits an alert when a label cardinality increase or new metric name exceeds threshold for a tenant.
4) Backfill job can replay a 7-day window with watermarking and idempotent writes; verified on staging.
5) Grafana dashboard queries show merged 50/90/99 latency percentiles by route and match trace-anchored percentiles within 2% for a test load.
6) No more than 5% additional p50 latency added at the ingest tier under production steady-state traffic.
7) Rollout plan with canary and rollback steps documented and validated in runbook.
notes: 2026-03-02: Spike completed; validated OTLP->envelope mapping with sample service (Aisha)
2026-03-04: Prototype dedupe using (request_id, trace_id, model_variant) keys; encountered high-cardinality tenant tag; need cardinality guard (Diego)
2026-03-06: Implemented deterministic hash-sample for low-value routes to preserve SLO signal for high-volume tenants (PR opened)
2026-03-09: Drift detector threshold proposed: 3x baseline cardinality increase OR 10k unique values in 1 hour for a tenant; pending security review for tenant-scoped metrics
2026-03-10: Integration tests added for Prometheus scrape adaptation; staging run shows 1.8% ingestion latency overhead at p50
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping and dedupe logic; integration tests that replay mixed OTLP + prometheus inputs; canary job in staging that replays 24h of production traffic into a sandbox KPI store and asserts idempotency; load test target: 50k envelopes/s sustained with 95th percentile processing latency < 200ms.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy Schema Guardian to infra namespace in canary region behind feature flag. 2) Route 2% of production traffic (tenant-based) for 24 hours and compare merged vs legacy metrics. 3) Increase to 10% for 48 hours, validate SLOs and backfill logic. 4) Full migration for non-critical tenants, then full traffic. 5) Rollback: switch ingress routing back to legacy adapters and replay suppression rules.
monitoring_and_alerts: Create Grafana panels for processing-latency, input-rate, dedupe-rate, rejected-envelopes, drift-alerts; alert when processing-latency p99 > 1s or rejected-envelopes rate > 0.1% for 5m; create automated ticketing link to oncall Slack channel.
security_considerations: The service handles tenant identifiers and request traces. Ensure KMS for any persisted request identifiers in long-term backfill queues; RBAC gating for read access to raw envelopes; privacy review to avoid storing PII in labels. Security gating required before production release.
outstanding_questions: What deterministic hashing salt should we use per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant collisions?
Should high-cardinality route labels be truncated or replaced with route hash in the canonical envelope?
Do we need a per-tenant opt-out for backfills that touch persisted request identifiers?
implementation_steps: 1. Adapter layer: OTLP and Prometheus->envelope mappers (team: ingest-adapters).
2. Dedupe engine: idempotent write layer using envelope key derivation (team: telemetry).
3. Drift detector: streaming job with cardinality sketches and alerting (team: telemetry).
4. Backfill/Replay: watermark-aware replayer with idempotent writes (team: ops).
5. Tracing hooks: insert request_id and trace_id at the earliest serving runtime boundary (team: runtime).
6. Dashboard queries and validation harness (team: observability).
final_notes: This ticket consolidates several past spikes into a single converged collection path. Keep changes behind feature flags and perform tenant-by-tenant validation to avoid unforeseen billing or SLO impacts.
